category_title: Students exhibiting inappropriate verbal behavior and noise-making in academic contexts
minimal_context: Desi is sitting at his desk working on independent textbook activities.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Desi, it is time to start your independent textbook activities at your desk.

STUDENT: (Makes a loud buzzing noise with his mouth) I don't want to do this.

TUTOR: Please stop making noise and look at your book.

STUDENT: Stop telling me what to do! You're always bothering me!

TUTOR: You need to finish your assignment right now.

STUDENT: Leave me alone! If you don't go away, I'm going to rip this textbook up!

options.A: Use differentiated teaching methods based on the student's individual ways of learning, including diverse methods for giving instructions and modifying the independent textbook activities based on his individual preferences during each session.
options.B: Ask the student to choose his own creative projects in place of the independent textbook activities, basing the tasks entirely on his personal strengths and interests to complete at his desk during each session.
options.C: Provide a tape recorder that sounds a bell every minute, prompting the student to record whether he had positive interactions (e.g., not arguing) by checking Yes or No on a sheet of paper at his desk, and give feedback regarding accuracy following each session.
options.D: Organize pedagogical practices and the classroom environment to meet the student's individual needs during independent textbook activities at his desk, rather than just focusing on his internal skills during each session.
